svg.title: Ordered pairs of the first 400 zeros of zeta
svg.text: Ordered pairs of the first 400 nontrivial zeros of zeta
Each ordered pair (rho, rho') sits at (delta1, delta2, s) = (Re rho - 1/2, Re rho' - 1/2, (gamma - gamma') log(gamma_min/2pi)/2pi), weight m(rho) m(rho').
Uncertified computation: all 400 zeros found simple and on the line; the measure lies on the s axis, no pair with 0 < |s| < 0.243 (atom 400 / 0).
A. Schematic of the coordinates; the data lie on the s axis
line delta = 0: the s axis, carries all the mass of these zeros
band 0 < |delta| < Delta: empty iff the gap hypothesis holds (unproved)
|delta| >= Delta: O(T^(1-c)) zeros up to height T (Carlson 1920)
Delta = 1/8 in the drawing is illustrative; zones by max(|delta1|, |delta2|)

polygon.title: Delta <= max|delta| < 3/8: O(T^(1-c)) zeros up to height T (Carlson 1920); empty for the 400 zeros here
band: 0 < max|delta| < Delta = 1/8 (illustrative); empty iff the gap hypothesis holds (unproved)

circle.title: the atom at the origin: diagonal mass sum m(rho)^2 = 400 (all simple), off-diagonal (distinct zeros, equal ordinates) = 0

svg.text: B. The on-line slice: integrated pair count per zero (log-log)
y(x) = #{ordered pairs of distinct zeros, 0 < |s| <= x} / 400,
s unfolded with the density at the smaller ordinate (as in spacings.tsv).
The small-x cubic law is the GUE prediction for zeta, not a theorem.
ordered pairs with 0 < |s| <= x, per zero
